newsitem.title: UK: World 96/97 coffee crop seen up at 96.45 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: World 96/97 coffee crop seen up at 96.45 mln bags.

text.p: World coffee production is seen at 96.45 million 60-kg bags in the 1996/97 crop year against 87.64 million in 1995/96, statistician FO Licht in a first estimate of world production on Tuesday.
Licht said an increase of nearly nine million bags on the weather-affected 1995/96 crop would still be lower than the likely world demand.

Licht gave no consumption data but the Association of Coffee Producing Countries at a meeting in Costa Rica earlier this month put consumption at 100 million bags against its forecast output of 99 million.
Licht said in view of the estimated production deficit, producers' hopes "for stable and even higher prices do not seem to be far fetched".
"The indications are that in 1996/97 producers will be able to continue their tight supply policy," it said.
"Even if these production forecasts should be exceeded, producers may hope that their retention scheme will prevent any sharp fall in prices," it said.
Licht said of the total crop, arabica coffee output could rise to 64.78 million bags in 1996/97 from 57.80 million in 1995/96.
Robusta production will rise to 31.67 million bags from 29.83 million in the same period.
Licht said output in top coffee grower Brazil is forecast at 26 million bags in 1996/97, up by more than 10 million on the weather-affected 1995/96 crop.
Financial problems are affecting the industry in Colombia and output is expected to drop to 11.5 million bags, down 1.4 million on the year.
Ethiopia is expected to produce around 3.9 million bags this season which will keep the country at the top of the African producers' list.
Ivory Coast and Uganda are expected to follow at 3.8 million and 3.6 million respectively.
Indonesia, Asia's top grower, is forecast to produce 7.5 million bags, an increase of more than one million bags as it recovers from two years of drought.
Vietnamese production is growing from strength to strength and the country is expected to harvest 4.3 million bags this season against 4.1 million last season.
